title: The trim bound: gaps of 0.5, 0.8 and 1.0 mm are sewn across, 1.2 mm and up are trimmed
description: Eight 5 x 5 mm red fill squares with gaps of 0.5, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.5, 1.8 and 2.0 mm: PE-DESIGN 11.50 sews the three shortest gaps across as plain stitches (no jump at all) and trims the four others (needle-to-needle moves of 2.42 mm and more). The squares' y position is OpenStitch's choice. The squares are drawn where PE-DESIGN's are (the bounds of each square's needle points in its file). Each square starts on its under sewing's edge run at the inset corner, 1 mm in from the top-left, and leaves at its top-right corner, in OpenStitch since #1088 as in PE-DESIGN, so the needle-to-needle moves are PE-DESIGN's: sqrt((gap + 1)^2 + 1) mm. Since #1246 the squares are imported from the SVG the reference was made from (an SVG rect starts at its top-left corner) onto a Custom Size page, as the reference's Design Settings had it: on a Custom Size page PE-DESIGN sews no stitch in place where a move lands (#1013), so after a trim it ties in with two needle points, 0.3 mm out and back, and before one it locks with two, 0.3 mm back and home.

evidence.note: PE-DESIGN 11.50 reference machine/machine-trim-bound.pes (pe-refs-3, 2026-10-28): 698 stitches, 4 trims on moves of 2.42, 2.69, 2.97 and 3.16 mm; the 0.5, 0.8 and 1.0 mm gaps have no jump.

references.make: Import an SVG (100 x 100 mm) with eight 5 x 5 mm red squares at x = 10, 15.5, 21.3, 27.3, 33.5, 40, 46.8, 53.8 mm (gaps 0.5, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.5, 1.8, 2.0 mm), as Fill Stitch at PE-DESIGN's import defaults (multi-needle machine type, Jump Stitch Trimming on); change nothing. Save with Save As as PES (PE-DESIGN 11's default PES version) under the file name given, and record the PE-DESIGN version, the date, the operating system and every setting you changed in compat/reference/MANIFEST.json (see docs/COMPATIBILITY_TESTS.md).

measurements.evidence: every interior move is a trimmed jump (as many moves as trims); a gap PE-DESIGN does not trim is sewn across as a stitch, never left as a plain jump
PE-DESIGN's count; the ties and locks hold its needle points, the rest is the under sewing's order and the fill's short rows (#1247)

PE-DESIGN 11.50, the first four squares, sewn as one part (gaps of 0.5, 0.8 and 1.0 mm sewn across): the tie-in's 0.3 mm step out is the first needle point, at (1.3,1.0) from the first square's corner, and the part ends at the fourth square's top-right corner (#1246)

PE-DESIGN 11.50, the fifth square: lands at its inset corner after the trim, ties in out and back (two needle points), and locks one step back and home at its top-right corner after a last stitch of 4.24 mm (#1246)
PE-DESIGN 11.50, the sixth square, as the fifth (#1246)
PE-DESIGN 11.50, the seventh square, as the fifth (#1246)
PE-DESIGN 11.50, the last square: ends where its fill ends, at its top-left corner, the imported outline's first point (#1246)
